site.name: Tidal Gateway, Seabridge Wharf
site.description: Brownfield coastal/estuarine development site on the foreshore of a tidal estuary, 200×150m. Site is low-lying (2.0–3.5 mAOD) with variable Made Ground overlying soft Estuarine Alluvium. Discontinuous Peat horizon present in the central-northern zone, indicative of former saltmarsh. River Terrace Gravel provides an intermediate founding horizon; London Clay underlies the full site at depth.
site.constraints:
Made ground not deeper than 2m
Peat only in central northern zone x:60-140, y:80-150
London Clay is below 8m depth throughout

geological_units.name: Made Ground
geological_units.description: Loose to firm brown sandy FILL with brick, concrete rubble, ash and timber fragments. Former wharf and industrial yard. Variable density (SPT N 4–10). Potential contamination; unsuitable as founding stratum. Maximum thickness 2m.

geological_units.name: Estuarine Alluvium
geological_units.description: Soft to firm grey-brown silty CLAY with occasional shell fragments and organic laminae. High plasticity (Ip 35–55%). Cu 10–30 kPa. Highly compressible; primary consolidation settlements of 50–200mm anticipated under imposed loads. Significant long-term secondary compression risk. Thickness 1–4m.

geological_units.name: Peat
geological_units.description: Very soft to soft dark brown/black PEAT with fibrous plant remains and woody inclusions. Holocene inter-tidal saltmarsh deposit. Highly compressible and creep-prone; Cu typically <10 kPa. SPT N 1–3. Thickness 0.3–1.5m. Confined to central-northern zone. Presents severe differential settlement and gas generation risk.

geological_units.name: River Terrace Gravel
geological_units.description: Dense to very dense sub-rounded flint GRAVEL in a coarse sandy matrix with occasional cobbles. Pleistocene river terrace deposit. SPT N 25–45. Thickness 2–5m. Good drainage and moderate bearing capacity; potential preferred founding horizon for lightly loaded structures. Groundwater likely to be encountered within or above this unit.

geological_units.name: London Clay
geological_units.description: Stiff to very stiff grey-blue fissured CLAY. Eocene London Clay Formation. High plasticity (Ip 40–70%). Cu 80–160 kPa, increasing with depth. SPT N 15–35. Susceptible to swelling on unloading and long-term creep on fissures. Reliable deep founding stratum for piled foundations. Top of unit consistently below 8m depth across site.
